$comment: DERIVED, not verbatim. Computed by this extraction, not in the source. Recipes are those of the Data Integrity cryptosuite documents (vc-di-eddsa eddsa-jcs-2022 and eddsa-rdfc-2022, vc-di-ecdsa ecdsa-rdfc-2019), which this source cites and does not define: proofConfig is the proof without proofValue, with the document's @context copied in; each of proofConfig and the unsecured document is canonicalized (JCS: sorted keys, no whitespace; RDFC: URDNA2015 via pyld 3.x with the data-integrity v2 context from the file whose SHA-256 the source prints); hashData = SHA-256(canonical proofConfig) || SHA-256(canonical document); Ed25519 over hashData, or ECDSA P-256 with SHA-256 over hashData, the 64-octet proofValue read as r||s. For a chain, the unsecured document of a proof with previousProof carries the proof it names as its proof member. RDFC and the contexts were fetched on 2026-11-07. Pass 2 (verify, 2026-11-07) checked this recipe against the cryptosuite Recommendations themselves, fetched that day: https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-di-eddsa/ (sha256 d404f372131a0e237d85aa3a6887aa54acadb862714d73e7b001ba789b5716eb) and https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-di-ecdsa/ (sha256 790f86cee2574a6398be9cc6794e01210ab40622a35ec514a1f043c344eec107), both W3C Recommendation 15 May 2025. Their Proof Configuration, Hashing and Proof Serialization algorithms state the recipe above, and verify-signatures.derived.py reproduces their test vectors (recipe_validation), so a fail below is a property of the example, not of the harness.
